interactions.summary: Jiang pushes a student's materialist logic into a deliberately ugly reductio, asking what could stop drunkenness, promiscuity, or murder if earthly pleasure were all that mattered.
A student reads Beatrice's answer that coerced souls still share responsibility when their will yields, because true will keeps resisting like fire rising upward.

Jiang translates the passage into his own language: if a person really wills something, no worldly force can finally stop that upward motion, and blaming coercion hides the fact that one also consented.
The reading moves to exemplars of intact will, and Jiang opens the Mucius story as his next concrete illustration of how radical action proves the difference between intact will and surrender.

speaker_notes.note: The packet includes an empty transcript segment inserted after the long reading span.

claims.claim: Jiang uses a hedonistic reductio to argue that a life organized only around temporary earthly pleasure cannot answer the moral question of what should restrain action.
Jiang says Beatrice's model means that as long as the will remains intact it behaves like fire ascending, and no force on earth can finally stop it.
Jiang says the abducted souls cannot fully blame force, because letting the soldiers take them back counted as agreement and therefore as a yielding of will.
Jiang introduces Mucius as a paradigm of intact will that will illustrate why radical action matters more than clever strategic calculation.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang rewrites Beatrice's doctrine into his own causal image: if the will is real, it rises like fire and the universe bends to make a path for it.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the universe will bend itself to accommodate you
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's sharpest compression of Jiang's will-metaphysics and carries forward the earlier Piccarda argument.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang exposes the student's materialism by escalating it all the way to drunkenness, casual killing, and the question of what would actually stop you.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The provocation makes the moral stakes of the Timaeus-versus-Dante discussion impossible to keep abstract.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The Dantean standard of a will so whole that external force cannot make it cooperate in wrongdoing.
The Roman exemplar Beatrice names and Jiang begins to narrate as a case of extraordinary will under mortal pressure.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet turns the Timaeus-materialist challenge back into Dante's coercion problem and then pivots from Piccarda to Mucius as Jiang's next will exemplar.
